tast: Split Test and TestCase. Historically, testing.Test is used for three purposes. - Test meta data written by test authors. - struct to execute a test scenario. - JSON protocol between tast command, local_test_runner and bundles. This CL split the first one from the remaining others. Now, testing/test.go contains the Test meta data for test authors, and its validation logic. Other code is moved to testing/test_case.go. CRAS: bt_device - Better handle BT audio profile drop This change fixes two things: (1) If BT headset connected, but not able to connect HFP/HSP until timeout, it shall eventually disconnect. (2) If BT headset connected and in use, then A2DP disconnects for some reason, the headset shall disconnect instead of fallback to use HFP/HSP. This change adds cras_bt_device_notify_profile_dropped() as a more generic function to handle unexpected profile drop, by scheduling a full suspend of BT device. We used to rely on the event when HFP AG is dropped and destroyed to send disconnect message to bluetoothd, to make sure the device state changed back to 'disconnected'. However this logic had a bug that if a headset never established an HFP AG, it could miss the disconnect message and leaving BT UI showing the headset still connected. BUG=chromium:755242, b:133790771 TEST=Use unittest to verify. What this change fixes is just difficult to reproduce. Change-Id: Ia7b7606bbb9dfb5cc704a859de143c66cd03829e Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1683754 Tested-by: Hsinyu Chao <hychao@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Hsinyu Chao <hychao@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Hsinyu Chao <hychao@chromium.org>

CRAS: bt_device - Consolidate code for bt device conflict check BT audio profile connect event could be sent to CRAS while a different headset is already in use. In this scenario we decide to remove the conflicting older headset so user always see the latest connected BT headset. Check commits fff3039fa and 6dce077a0 for more background. In the beginning we use a iodev append callback to dedupe the HFP AG and devices that has previously connected. Later we added periodic watch callback and create another check to dedupe HFP/HSP only headset. Code becomes complicated because similar purpose code lives in two places. We should fix that. This change refactors the code by giving more responsibility to the periodic watch callback, to examine all conflicting headset cases. The append iodev callback is not needed anymore, since the watch callback works better for handling asynchronous events.
